As the parameter race among foundational models like Baidu's ERNIE, Alibaba's Tongyi, and Tencent's Hunyuan subsided, and the "hundred-model war" evolved into "industry-wide applications," companies suddenly realized that computing power, once considered mere infrastructure, had become the decisive factor in application deployment. The issue wasn't a lack of computing power, but the inability to find "just-right" computing power; not insufficient computing power, but wasted resources from "misallocated" computing power; not unaffordable computing power, but the cost of "ineffective usage" eroding profits. Oracle's $300 billion computing power deal with OpenAI also signaled industry changes: this wasn't merely "selling computing power" but an "ecosystem partnership." OpenAI requires Oracle's massive-scale computing clusters to support GPT-5's training and inference, while Oracle secures its computing demand for the next decade by aligning with a leading model company. This reflects two core trends in the global computing power market: first, "computing demand shifting from concentration to explosion." Large model training demands immense computing power (GPT-5 requires 10 times the computing power of GPT-3), while inference for applications like multimodal systems and AI agents grows exponentially. For instance, a live-streaming AI controller handling video streams, speech recognition, and audience interaction simultaneously consumes vastly more inference computing power than ordinary tasks.

items.title: Show HN: I made a heatmap diff viewer for code reviews
items.raw_excerpt: 0github.com is a pull request viewer that color-codes every diff line/token by how much human attention it probably needs. Unlike PR-review bots, we try to flag not just by "is it a bug?" but by "is it worth a second look?" (examples: hard-coded secret, weird crypto mode, gnarly logic, ugly code). To try it, replace github.com with 0github.com in any pull-request URL. Under the hood, we split the PR into individual files, and for each file, we ask an LLM to annotate each line with a data structure that we parse into a colored heatmap. excerpt_i18n.en: On October 18, Chery officially held the 2025 Global Technology Innovation Conference in Wuhu. At the opening, Yin Tongyue, Chairman of Chery Automobile Co., Ltd., declared a somewhat familiar statement: This year, we will boldly proclaim that Chery's global innovation system will also 'not hold back.' It has almost become a tradition for Chery to use the phrase 'not hold back' at innovation conferences, but in reality, the company has been growing rapidly in recent years. In 2024, Chery's global passenger vehicle sales totaled 74.3 million units, ranking among the world's top 20 automakers with 2.295 million units sold and achieving the highest year-on-year growth rate of 49.4% on the list. Additionally, Chery has gained significant presence in overseas markets, covering 120 countries and regions with over 5.5 million cumulative users, and it has led China's passenger vehicle exports for 22 consecutive years. In 2025, its PHEV models ranked first in market share in eight countries, including Chile, the UAE, and Thailand, with projected sales in the European market reaching 80,000 units. However, in today's highly competitive market, Chery clearly cannot afford to relax. At this conference, Chery introduced five core technology areas: Mars Architecture, Kunpeng Power, Lingxi Smart Cabin, Falcon Intelligent Driving, and Galaxy Ecosystem. At the architectural level, Mars Architecture serves as an underlying platform covering all brands and powertrain types, flexibly adaptable for sedans, SUVs, MPVs, and crossovers, with core technologies focused on electronic architecture and chassis systems.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 18 de octubre, Chery celebró oficialmente en Wuhu la Conferencia Global de Innovación Tecnológica 2025. Al inicio, Yin Tongyue, presidente de Chery Automobile Co., Ltd., declaró una frase algo familiar: "Este año, proclamamos con fuerza: el sistema de innovación global de Chery también 'no se andará con contemplaciones'". Parece haberse convertido en una tradición que Chery anuncie "no andarse con contemplaciones" en estas conferencias, pero los hechos muestran un crecimiento acelerado en los últimos dos años. En 2024, las ventas globales de vehículos de pasajeros de Chery alcanzaron los 74,30 millones de unidades, posicionándose entre los 20 mayores fabricantes mundiales con 2,295 millones de vehículos vendidos y ocupando el primer lugar en la lista con una tasa de crecimiento interanual del 49,4%.
